name: Collabicle
tagline: Bundled team workspace: tasks, boards, docs and files in one place instead of four tabs.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Every all-in-one workspace is really five CRUD apps sharing a sidebar, and CRUD is exactly what coding agents are good at. A single-user version with projects, a kanban board, nested docs, comments and file attachments is a weekend of work, and if you are the only person using it you will not miss much. The gaps show up the moment a second human logs in: accounts, roles, invites, realtime cursors, notification email, an audit trail of who changed what. Mobile is a separate project entirely, and so is every integration you currently take for granted. If the product is doing real coordination work across a team, keep paying; if you adopted it as a fancy personal to-do list with docs attached, build it.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app with projects, drag-and-drop task boards, markdown docs nested under projects, comments, and file uploads, all in one SQLite file.
requirements: a machine that stays on if you want it reachable from a phone browser
Tailscale or similar if you want access away from home
whatYouLose: Multiplayer: realtime editing, presence, and conflict handling on shared docs
Accounts, roles and permissions, so nothing is safely shareable with a client or contractor
Native mobile and push notifications; you get a browser tab that forgets you
Integrations: calendar, Slack, email-to-task, Drive, webhooks, whatever glue you currently rely on
Search that stays fast and useful once you have thousands of items, plus backups and version history someone else worries about
moatNotes: The moat is other people already being in there. A workspace nobody else can open is a notebook.
whyPeopleStillPay: All-in-one suites sell the absence of decisions. The paying customer is usually a small team lead who does not want to pick a task tool, a docs tool, a file tool and then wire them together, and who definitely does not want to be the person maintaining the wiring. The per-seat bill buys onboarding for people who will never read a README, an audit trail when a deadline slips, and someone to email when the database is unreachable. None of that matters to a solo user, which is why the honest answer here splits so hard by headcount.
notes: Bundled suites are the easiest category to half-replace and the hardest to fully replace, because the missing half is your coworkers.
prompt:
Build a single-user, self-hosted team-workspace clone called Hive. Local only, no cloud services, no telemetry, no sign-up flow.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, React Server Components where sensible
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, schema managed with Drizzle ORM, one file at ./data/hive.db
- Tailwind CSS for styling, dnd-kit for drag and drop
- Server Actions for all mutations, no separate REST layer
- File uploads written to ./data/uploads, served through a route handler

Data model: workspaces have projects; projects have tasks, docs and files. Task fields: title, markdown body, status (todo/doing/blocked/done), priority, due date, labels (many-to-many), order index. Docs: title, markdown body, optional parent doc for nesting, updatedAt. Comments attach polymorphically to tasks or docs. Full-text search across task titles, task bodies and doc bodies using SQLite FTS5.

Screens:
1. Sidebar shell listing projects, plus a global search box (cmd+k) that queries FTS5.
2. Project board: kanban columns by status, drag to reorder and move, inline create, optimistic UI.
3. Task detail as a right-side drawer: markdown editor with live preview, labels, due date, comments, file attachments.
4. Docs tree per project with a two-pane markdown editor, autosave every 2 seconds, keep the last 20 revisions in a revisions table with a diff view.
5. Today view: tasks due today or overdue across all projects.

In scope: keyboard shortcuts for new task and search, dark mode, a /api/export route that dumps everything as JSON plus markdown files, a seed script with two projects and about thirty tasks.

Out of scope, do not build: authentication, users, roles, invites, realtime collaboration, email, notifications, chat, mobile apps, third-party integrations, billing.

Secrets: none needed, but read PORT and DATA_DIR from .env with sane defaults and commit .env.example only.

Deliver a README with setup, a single `npm run dev` that migrates and seeds on first boot, and a short note on backing up hive.db and the uploads folder.
